about: Provenance of every transform in magpie/cwplans, modelled on W3C PROV (prov:Activity used / generated). Checked and exported to pipeline.jsonld by tools/check-data-register.mjs. Edit by hand when a tool changes.
conventions: Paths are relative to magpie/cwplans. "file" = tracked in git; "local" = not committed (gitignored raw data, caches, excluded outputs, or files a tool takes as arguments); "source" = a key of data-register.json sources. A source entry with "access": "manual download" means the file was downloaded by hand before the run and the tool reads only the local copy. Read from the code on 2026-10-03. "area" is a key of "areas" (the sections of METHODS.md); "faults" are F-numbers of the fault register in skills/docklands-data-curation/SKILL.md; "judgement" says where a hand decision enters and where it is recorded. "manual_activities" are methods that are not tools (hand curation, research catalogues, licence decisions); "gap" says what of a method is not committed as code.

activities.method: Builds the corridor model (Canada Water): a 10 m terrain grid, building footprints with heights, water levels, railways with tunnel chains and open cuts, roads, and stations and Wikidata places, in local metres around E0 535400, N0 179400.
rules: Terrain: median of the DTM in a 7 x 7 m window every 10 m.

Building height: OSM height tag; else the 90th percentile of DSM - DTM inside the footprint (at least 6 cells, at least 2 m) unless it is under half of building:levels x 3 m; else building:levels x 3 m + 1 m ('newer' when LiDAR exists); else the LiDAR value; else 6 m (0 for building=construction).
Buildings: centroid inside the box with a 2 m margin; single-outer multipolygons only.
Water: natural=water, waterway=dock or landuse=basin over 50 m2; level = 25th percentile of the DTM inside.
Tunnel portals: tunnel nodes shared with an open railway way, at the open track level (DSM on bridges, DTM otherwise).
Open cut: a tunnel point where the DTM is more than 6 m below the ground 25-35 m around; each run of cut points takes its lowest bed.
Published levels from data/sourced-levels.json are applied to the nearest tunnel point within 150 m (lib.mjs applyControls); superseded controls are skipped.
Places: OSM railway=station nodes, then Wikidata items of a fixed list of transport, water and landform classes that are not already a station.
Coordinates: WGS84 to BNG through OSTN15 (tools/lib.mjs bngProjector); local metres x = E - 535400, z = -(N - 179400); heights in metres above Ordnance Datum Newlyn.
Rounding: geometry in whole decimetres, delta-encoded (tools/lib.mjs enc); heights and levels to 0.1 m (r1); control levels to 0.01 m.
activities.judgement: The published levels in data/sourced-levels.json are chosen by hand (manual activity sourced-levels).

used.request: two chart-datum-to-ODN offsets written into the code: 3.20 m at London Bridge, 3.35 m at North Woolwich

activities.method: Builds the Docklands 3D model (terrain, water, greens, buildings and parts, roads, railways, tunnels, places, flood defences, riverbed) into area.js, and the Canary Wharf underground detail (basements, indoor ways, level-tagged points, published structures) into under.js, in local metres around E0 537550, N0 180300.
rules: Terrain: median of the DTM in a 7 x 7 m window every 20 m.

Building height: OSM height; else LiDAR 90th percentile of DSM - DTM (at least 6 cells, at least 2 m) unless under half of building:levels x 3 m; else Wikidata P2048 (outlines only); else building:levels x 3 m + 1 m ('newer' when LiDAR exists); else LiDAR; else 6 m (0 for construction, roof, ruins).
An outline that contains building parts is drawn by its parts; a part's base is its min_height, else building:min_level x 3 m.
Outside the Canary Wharf focus box, outlines under 12 m2 are dropped and rings are simplified at 0.6 m (0.2 m inside).
Basements: OSM building:levels:underground, else Wikidata P1139.
Floors (focus box only): OSM building:levels (minus building:min_level on a part), else Wikidata P1101.
Water level: 25th percentile of the DTM inside the area; areas under 40 m2 (water) or 300 m2 (greens) are dropped.
Bridge points more than 20 m above the DTM are taken as covered by a roof and interpolated from the nearest uncovered points on the same way.
Tunnel chains for rail, road and foot tunnels; portals at the open level; open cut where the DTM is more than 6 m below the ground 25-35 m around.
Riverbed: each UKHO sounding in the box as z_cd minus the chart datum offset interpolated by longitude between 3.20 m and 3.35 m.
Flood defence crest: actual_ucl, else actual_dcl, else design_ucl; lines without a crest are dropped.
Published levels from data/sourced-levels.json are tunnel controls (nearest point within 150 m); structures with footprint_osm or water_name are drawn from their OSM way or water area.
Wikidata places: classes matching the KEEP pattern; classes matching memorial, war memorial, grave or cemetery are left out.
Level tags are read by tools/osm-values.mjs osmLevels.
Coordinates: WGS84 to BNG through OSTN15; local metres x = E - 537550, z = -(N - 180300) (ORIGIN, One Canada Square to about 20 m); heights in metres above Ordnance Datum Newlyn.
Rounding: geometry in whole decimetres, delta-encoded (tools/lib.mjs enc); heights to 0.1 m; control levels to 0.01 m.
Fixed faults (F10): simplify() splits a closed ring at its farthest point before Douglas-Peucker; bridge points under a roof are interpolated.
activities.judgement: The published levels in data/sourced-levels.json are chosen by hand (manual activity sourced-levels); the KEEP class list for Wikidata places is written in the tool.

activities.method: Reads the OSM business features of the Canary Wharf box (osm-scan) and keeps those that are branches of a brand: by the feature's brand:wikidata, by the NSI Matcher on its names under its own key=value at its position, or by a brand tag that NSI does not list; street furniture is counted apart.
rules: A business feature is a branch when (1) its brand:wikidata is an NSI UK brand QID, or (2) the NSI Matcher matches its name, brand, name:en or official_name under its own key=value at its position, or (3) it has brand or brand:wikidata that NSI does not list.
For a QID with several NSI items, the item whose key=value agrees with the feature is preferred.
Disused features and opening_hours=closed are skipped.
Street furniture (post boxes, ATMs, bicycle rental, lockers, vending machines and similar) is counted apart, not as branches.

Name fields are tried in the order name, brand, name:en, official_name; the first NSI hit with match "primary" wins, else the first hit of any kind (alternate hits are accepted here, unlike the FSA match).
The NSI Matcher is asked at the feature's own position (lon, lat), not at a fixed point.
A conflict between the OSM brand:wikidata and the NSI QID is kept and flagged (qid_conflict); fhrs:id, addr:*, level, level:ref and website are carried for the later joins.
Named businesses that match no brand are listed apart (unmatched_named_business), not dropped silently.

Two named malls decide a join by themselves; Canada Place and One Canada Square count as one level.
An OSM feature whose fhrs:id equals the FSA premises id is the same branch.
Wikidata items join a branch within 300 m.

A CWG entry needs an NSI match (or a decision in cwg-decisions.json); a 'prefix' or 'alternate' match or a type that does not fit the CWG section is left undecided; otherwise a CWG title that names a branch already found (5 or more letters, whole words) joins it.
Postcode to mall: kept when 4 or more CWG entries share the postcode and 85% or more name the same mall.
Position: OSM feature, else FSA geocode, else mall centre or ONSPD postcode centroid (flagged).
Confidence: high with two or more sources; low for a single prefix or alternate FSA match or a note that says low confidence; else medium.
Category from the key=value (bank, pharmacy, supermarket, cafe, takeaway, restaurant, bar, gym, hotel, leisure, health, childcare, office, motoring, service, shop, other).

rules: Skipped: FSA ratings pages (data from the FSA API), OSM, Wikidata, Companies House and Land Registry links (data from their APIs or bulk files), Wikipedia (CC BY-SA, share-alike), canarywharf.com pages with no archived copy (the live site answers scripts with an Imperva challenge).
A canarywharf.com URL is replaced by its Internet Archive copy from cwg-directory.json.
robots.txt per RFC 9309: the group for 'glitchcan-cwplans', else '*'; longest match wins, Allow wins a tie; a 4xx robots.txt allows all; a 5xx or unreachable robots.txt disallows all.

Failure classes: robots disallowed, robots unreachable, bot challenge (Cloudflare, Imperva, Akamai, DataDome, PerimeterX pages), 401/403 refused, 404/410 not found, 4xx other, 429, 5xx, timeout, dns, tls, connection, not HTML, too many redirects.

Kept per page: schema.org name, telephone, address, geo, opening hours, price range, cuisine, menu, sameAs, reservations; events with name, dates, location, URL; page title and OpenGraph title/type (cut to 200 characters), OpenGraph description cut to 200 characters; html lang; feed and link URLs. No other page text.

names_branch: true when the entry's postcode is in the page text or structured data, or an address phrase (street, mall, branch name) is on a page that is not the site's home page; 'home page lists the place' when only a phrase is on a home page; 'scripts only' when the match is only inside page scripts.
A URL with a stored result is not fetched again (--refresh fetches all; --retry-failed fetches transient failures again).
At most 8 redirects (MAX_REDIRECTS); the backoff waits Retry-After when given, else 4, 12, 36 s.
Owner rule 2026-10-03: website crawls, direct and through the Internet Archive or Common Crawl, are fair use for scoping (CLAUDE.md, cwplans exception).

activities.method: Renders every web page the registry links to in headless Chromium and extracts from the rendered DOM: every JSON-LD script text as found, microdata (WHATWG algorithm) as JSON, and RDFa 1.1 as N-Triples. The same extractor runs over the server HTML of the same visit with scripts off, to mark blocks that only scripts made. For chain branches with no store page, searches the brand's store finder with the branch postcode and renders the branch page it links to.
rules: Skipped: FSA ratings pages, OSM, Wikidata, Wikipedia (CC BY-SA), Companies House, Land Registry, register pages, social networks, the live canarywharf.com (Imperva challenge).
robots.txt per RFC 9309 (token glitchcan-cwplans, else *); an unreachable robots.txt means no visit; the failure is classed by its cause (dns, tls, timeout, 5xx).
Order: store pages, then pages the plain crawl got no structured data from, then the rest; Internet Archive CWG copies read from cache with scripts off.
A cookie banner is clicked only when the page shows no structured data and a known consent button is visible. No logins, no forms other than a store-finder search box with a UK postcode.
Store finder: a result link is followed only when its text, URL or card names the branch postcode, a street or mall phrase of the branch, or (for a brand with one branch here) Canary Wharf.
Blocks over 200 kB are dropped and counted.
User-Agent: a desktop Chrome string plus " glitchcan-cwplans/0.1 (+https://github.com/danbri/glitchcan-minigam)"; robots.txt fetched with Node (15 s timeout), else through Chromium.
Each page: wait for load and network idle, at most 20 s (CAP_MS), then 1.5 s (LATE_MS) for late JSON-LD.

Store finders: one postcode search per brand and postcode; the postcode is the branch's own, else E14 4QT (owner rule 2026-10-03: "we are permitted per industry convention to submit storefinder forms with UK postcodes"). No other forms.
Resumable: a URL with a stored result in data/raw/rendered/ is not rendered again unless --retry-failed and its failure was transient.
activities.judgement: The skip list and the consent-button list are written in the tool; store-finder searches follow the owner rule of 2026-10-03.

used.request: jsonldToRdf, parse (N-Triples, N-Quads), query (SPARQL 1.1 SELECT over named graphs)

activities.method: Cleans each JSON-LD block (jsonld-clean.mjs: wrappers, comments, trailing and missing commas, control characters, invalid escapes, concatenated values, HTML entities, remote schema.org contexts inlined as {"@vocab": "https://schema.org/"}, @graph unwrapped, http://schema.org/ normalised; every repair counted by class), converts it with Factoidal jsonldToRdf, converts microdata JSON to RDF (schema.org vocabulary), parses RDFa N-Triples with Factoidal, loads one named graph per page, writes all.nq, then runs SPARQL with Factoidal for types, names, telephones, opening hours and their specifications, addresses, geo and events, and attributes each node to the registry entities that link to the page.
rules: Scope branch, confidence high: the node's postcode equals the entity's, or its geo is within 300 m of the building.
Scope branch, confidence medium: the node has no address and the page is the branch's own page (a store_url field, a store-finder result, or a URL path that names the place).
Scope branch, confidence low: the node's postcode is another E14/E20 postcode (a sibling branch is possible).
Scope chain: a chain branch's general page with no address on the node (chain-wide facts, not branch facts). Scope organisation: the same for a non-chain entity's own site.
Nodes with an address or position elsewhere are not attributed and are counted.

Opening hours to OSM opening_hours: days grouped, 23:59 closes become 24:00, opens = closes = 00:00 is 'off', dated specifications become date-range rules; unparsed text is kept raw with the problem listed.

activities.method: Builds the Canary Wharf building registry: one record per OSM building outline with a stable cwb- id, its parts, occupants (OSM, FSA, Wikidata, chain-store branches, the Canary Wharf Group directory, the regulatory and public registers), owners, postcodes, Wikidata facts, and company and property joins.
rules: A building is an OSM building outline (way or multipolygon) whose vertex mean is in the Canary Wharf box; building:part shapes are listed under the outline that contains their centre.
Ids: reused from registry/ids.json by OSM element; new outlines get the next number in reading order (north to south in 100 m bands, then west to east); a retired id is never reused.

OSM occupants: named features with a shop, food and drink, office, amenity, leisure, tourism, healthcare, craft or transport role, placed in the outline that contains them or the nearest outline within 12 m; artworks, information boards, viewpoints and attractions are features, not occupants. Each OSM occupant keeps its tags opening_hours, cuisine, wheelchair, check_date, start_date, opening_date, operator, url, level, brand, brand:wikidata, website (or contact:website), phone (or contact:phone), email (or contact:email) and the other contact:* links (as contact).
FSA premises with a position in the box are placed the same way; the others are listed under their postcode when its tier is cw-*.

Wikidata: an OSM wikidata tag wins; else the one building-like item whose coordinate is in the outline (within 5 m) and no other building-like item is inside it; an item already named by an OSM tag is not attached to a second outline; other items inside are occupants 'located here'.
The Wikidata label replaces the OSM name; the OSM name is kept as osm_name.
Owners: Wikidata P127. Occupants also from P466 and from organisations whose P159 is the building.
UPRN points inside the outline (no tolerance) give UPRN counts, TOIDs and USRNs; LBSM2 homes are summed over the building's TOIDs.
Home figures are given only where at least 5 homes are counted (K = 5); otherwise 'fewer than 5'.
INSPIRE polygons that contain the building's centre are linked by INSPIRE id.

Companies and price-paid sales join a building when the postcode is one of its postcodes and the normalised address contains one of its keys (address, name, OSM name, Wikidata street address), and exactly one building matches.
A residential building lists only the count of registered companies, not their names.
Branches enrich the occupant with the same OSM or FSA id, else are placed by position (marked approximate when the position is a mall or postcode centre).
Buildings keep the OSM addr:housename (housename): it names the complex for a mall outline (Canada Place on 16-19 Canada Square).

CWG directory: an entry already linked by the branch join keeps that link. Else it joins existing occupants (OSM, FSA, Wikidata, branches, and CWG occupants added earlier in the same pass) when a name key is equal (registry/sources/brands/tools/cwg-fields.mjs nameKeys) and the place agrees, tried in this order: same mall (or same street or square), a shared postcode, or the building the entry itself would be placed in. Two different named malls never join (Canada Place and the One Canada Square mall count as one). An occupant with a CWG link takes a second entry only from another CWG section (cwg_also). Records of one source in two buildings: ambiguous, not joined.

CWG entries that join nothing become occupants (source cwg, role directory: <section>) placed by: the one building whose address key equals the street line (confidence high with the postcode, medium without); else the host outline of a named mall (the one outline whose OSM name, else addr:housename, is the mall name or starts with it; medium); else the one registry building with the entry postcode, or the one of them OSM tags as retail (low). Estate-wide entries, car parks and entries with no page, address or single building stay unplaced with a reason (cwg_unplaced, summary.joins.cwg).

Registers (registry/sources/registers/): records are excluded when the address is not a place: GIAS correspondence addresses (address_role), the registered-office service at E14 5HU / 10th floor 5 Churchill Place, care-of and accountant addresses. Keys in order: UPRN (OS Open UPRN point inside an outline; not used when one register gives the UPRN to records at two or more postcodes, or when the UPRN point is over 150 m from the register point), the register point (inside or within 12 m; an FSA point within 3 m of its postcode centre is a postcode, F7), a named mall in the address (the mall host outline, F4; the point outline kept as point_in), street address with the postcode, street address alone when one building matches a numbered address key, the name of an occupant at the same postcode or mall, the postcode alone when one registry building has it, the ONSPD centre is within 50 m of it and the address names no other street (never for a charity). A charity placed by address in a residential building (homes or a residential building tag) is left unplaced. A record whose name matches an occupant of the chosen building enriches it; else it is a new occupant (source = register, role register: <name> or head office (ODS) for ODS organisation records, current false for closed or inactive records). Each link (occupant.registers[]) keeps register, id, kind, status, key, precision, confidence; source ids are copied to the occupant (urn, ods_code, cqc_location_id, charity_number, company_number, ofsted_urn, gambling_premises_id, active_places_site_id, fhrs_id). Unplaced records and rejected UPRNs are listed (registers_unplaced, registers_uprn_rejected).

activities.method: Adds the facts read from the entities' own web pages (schema.org opening hours, telephone, events, menu, price range, cuisine) to the building occupants as occupants[].web, with the page, the fetch date, the scope and the confidence of the match.
rules: Keys: "cwb-NNNN|name" (occupant name in that building, case and accents folded), "branch:<brand QID>@<element>" (the occupant's OSM element, the building's OSM way, fhrs/<FSA id> or a bare FSA id, cwg/<slug>), "charity:<number>", "cwg:<directory slug>".
One record per occupant: branch scope beats organisation beats chain; then high, medium, low confidence.
A fact record with no hours, phone, events, menu, price range or cuisine is not joined; records that match no occupant are counted (summary.joins.web_facts).
Run after build-registry (which rewrites buildings.json without web facts) and before build-categories and build-atlas.

activities.method: Gives each registry building its occupant categories (finance, shop, catering, leisure, entertainment; and bar, alcohol, education, health, sport, arts, charity) from the classes the sources state, for the glow outlines and the atlas.
rules: finance: OSM amenity bank, bureau_de_change or money_transfer, or office financial, insurance, financial_advisor or tax_advisor; or a Wikidata P31 or P452 label matching bank, finance, insurance, investment and similar; or the role 'service: bank' or 'branch: bank'.
shop: an OSM shop tag, the role 'shop' or 'branch: shop', or an FSA type starting 'Retailers'.
catering: OSM amenity restaurant, cafe, bar, pub, fast_food, food_court, ice_cream or biergarten; the role 'food and drink' or a food branch; or an FSA catering type.
leisure: OSM leisure fitness_centre, sports_centre, swimming_pool, sauna, dance or sports_hall; a hotel role or FSA hotel type.
entertainment: OSM cinema, theatre, nightclub, arts centre, casino, events or music venue, planetarium, amusement and bowling leisure, museum or gallery; or a Wikidata class matching those.
bar: OSM amenity pub, bar, nightclub or biergarten; FSA type Pub/bar/nightclub; CWG category Bars or Cocktails; a Wikidata class pub, bar, nightclub.
alcohol: OSM shop alcohol, wine or beverages.

education: OSM amenity school, college, university, kindergarten or childcare; FSA type School/college/university; CWG category Childcare; a Wikidata class school, university, college, academic institution, kindergarten or nursery; the role branch: childcare.

health: OSM amenity doctors, dentist, pharmacy, clinic or hospital, or any healthcare tag; CWG category Healthcare unless OSM says amenity=veterinary; a Wikidata class hospital, clinic, doctor's office, medical organization, dental, pharmacy.

sport: OSM leisure sports_centre, fitness_centre, pitch, swimming_pool or sports_hall, or any sport tag; CWG category Sport (not Sport & Fitness, which lists sportswear shops); a Wikidata sports venue or gym class; the role branch: gym.

arts: OSM amenity cinema, theatre, arts_centre, nightclub, music_venue, events_venue or concert_hall, or any theatre:genre tag; a Wikidata class movie theater, cinema, theatre, music venue, concert hall, arts centre or nightclub.

CWG directory classes for the first five: section restaurant gives catering, section stay or category Hotels & Apartments gives leisure, category Banks & Foreign Exchange gives finance, and goods categories (Shoes & Footwear, Menswear, Jewellery & Watches and others listed in the tool) give shop. CWG labels that mix classes (Services, Health & Beauty, Cafes & Bars, Sport & Fitness) and the FSA type Hospitals/Childcare/Caring Premises are not used.

Registers (current links only): GIAS, Ofsted childcare and ODS School give education; CQC health services (doctors, dentists, diagnosis, urgent care, clinics, hospitals, community healthcare, nursing homes) and ODS service sites (pharmacies, surgeries, GP practices, dental practices, optical sites, NHS trust, independent provider, PCT and care trust sites) give health; Active Places gives sport; FSA pubs give bar; gambling premises (betting shops) give shop; the Charity Commission gives charity. ODS organisation records, ODS Education (NHS training bodies) and social care services give no category. An occupant with current false counts as former.
Names are never used to guess a class; Companies House registered offices are not used.

Wikidata occupant links: an end date (P582) or a dissolved organisation (P576) makes the entry 'former' and it is not counted; a start date and no end makes it 'current'; no qualifier makes it 'undated'.

rules: Stars: Bright Star Catalogue rows with a J2000 position and V <= 5.5 (2,887); columns from the CDS ReadMe: HR 1-4, RA 76-83, Dec 84-90, Vmag 103-107, B-V 110-114; RA and Dec to 0.001 degree, V and B-V to 0.01; a missing B-V becomes 0.6; sorted by V.

Constellation lines: every line string kept; longitude turned into RA 0-360 degrees; coordinates rounded to 0.01 degree. The Milky Way outlines of the same repository are not fetched (no stated licence); the page computes the band from galactic coordinates.

Satellites: the three requests merged, one record per NORAD catalogue number; OMM fields kept as published. CelesTrak keeps no history, so a snapshot holds the elements current at fetch time (run within a day or two of the date). One request per group per run (CelesTrak: at most one download per 2 hours).
Weather: the forecast API's past hours (best_match model, UK Met Office UKV first for London; it has visibility, which the ERA5 archive lacks); values as published, hourly, London time.

Tide: 15-minute instantaneous readings in m AOD, UTC times, sorted; no gap filling; EA gives readings only, no predictions. The page (sky.js cleanGauges) leaves out a reading whose difference from the nearest other gauge departs more than 0.45 m from the median of that difference over 2 h either side (fault F21), then interpolates linearly by chainage along data/river.json between the gauges. The EA has no tidal gauge between Tower Pier and Charlton (station search of 2026-10-04, 15 km round the estate).

Star names: rows of IAU-CSN whose designation is an HR number present in stars.json (324 of 451 names); columns found by the positions of the header titles (Name/Diacritics, Designation, Con), because names can hold spaces; the diacritic form is kept.

Clouds: the EUMETSAT cloud mask PNG kept as sent. The page (sky.js) reads white pixels (R, G, B > 200) as cloud, takes the mean over 60 km round the box centre, and raises each layer's Open-Meteo cover by 0.9 x (local mask - mean), clamped to 0..1, so the mask places the cloud and Open-Meteo keeps the amount; the mask moves with 2.2 x the 10 m wind for up to 90 minutes from its slot. Other times only with Fetch ticked (EUMETView sends CORS headers; the mask appears about 25 minutes after the slot; none before 2020-09-01). Parallax (about 1.6 km north for cloud at 1 km over London) is not corrected.

Messier: all 109 rows of the HEASARC table (M 102 is not in it); RA and Dec from sexagesimal J2000 to degrees (0.001); size = the larger dimension in arcmin; the notes column title-cased as the common name. OpenNGC was not used (CC BY-SA).
Network: User-Agent glitchcan-cwplans/0.1; three retries 3, 6 and 9 s apart on timeouts and 5xx (the agent proxy drops connections now and then); 4xx is not retried; files overwritten on every run.

activities.method: Walks the London Datastore (a DataPress site with a CKAN-compatible API): reads the whole catalogue from the v3 export, writes it compact (one dataset per line); triages every dataset by written rules (licence class, relevance to the zone, kind, whether the project already holds or lists it, value themes, join keys, sensitivity, score); harvests the shortlisted open datasets and keeps the features that meet the 3D model box, as GeoJSON in WGS84 with a meta member (source, URLs, fetch date, licence, attribution, method, counts).
rules: Catalogue: publisher = organisation (logo title), else CKAN maintainer, else custom.author; geo = custom.geo (spatial granularity); update_frequency = custom.update_frequency; resource format = file extension; resource URL = https://data.london.gov.uk/download/{dataset}/{id}/{file}. Not kept: descriptions, contact names and emails, logos.

Licence class: OGL v2/v3 -> ogl; Creative Commons Attribution -> cc-by; ODC Attribution -> odc-by; Public Domain, PDDL -> public-domain (these four are open); CC BY-SA and ODbL -> share-alike (never harvested, CLAUDE.md); CC Non-Commercial and All Rights Reserved -> restricted; TfL Transport Data Service Licence -> other; empty -> none (never harvested).

Relevance, first match: zone-place (title or tag names a place in the 3D model box; "upon Thames", "Thames Estuary", "Thames Gateway", "Thamesmead" removed first); zone-borough (names only Tower Hamlets, Southwark, Lewisham, Greenwich, Newham, City of London); other-area (names 1-3 places, none in the zone); london-fine (geo finer than a borough, or with no geo a ward/LSOA/MSOA/OA/postcode/UPRN/TOID word or a spatial format); london-borough; london-coarse; unknown.

Have: a dataset id or slug in a committed file of magpie/cwplans: data-register.json, pipeline.json, tools, data files -> held; a .md note, feeds catalogues, the 2026-10-03 survey -> listed; an "excluded" list or a survey "left out" line -> excluded-before; else new. feeds/london-datastore/ and the generated docs are not read.

Sensitive (catalogued, score 0, never harvested): title names homicide, victims, strip or intimate searches, suicide, custody, stop and search, hate crime, domestic abuse, sexual offences, safeguarding, missing persons, rough sleeping (CHAIN), bariatric incidents.

Score = relevance weight (zone-place 5, zone-borough 4, london-fine 3, london-borough 1.5, unknown 1, london-coarse 0.3, other-area 0) x max(theme value, 0.5) x recency (newest resource year >= 2024: 1, >= 2021: 0.8, >= 2016: 0.5, else 0.3) x (machine-readable format ? 1 : 0.4) x (a join key finer than a borough ? 1.3 : 1) x (open ? 1 : 0) x (held 0, listed 0.8, new 1).

Harvest zone: a feature is kept when its geometry meets the 3D model box (BNG E 532400-539900, N 176700-182300): a vertex inside, an edge crossing (Liang-Barsky) or the box centre inside a polygon. Whole geometries kept, not cut; whole_in_zone and in_cw (meets the Canary Wharf registry box -0.03, 51.498, -0.005, 51.51) are added.

Coordinates: GeoPackage SRS 27700, or a custom definition on Airy 1830 with the BNG projection (srs_id 100000) -> BNG; output WGS84 to 6 decimal places through OSTN15. CSV points: a row is WGS84 when |x| <= 180 and |y| <= 90, else BNG; empty or zero coordinates -> no_geometry.

Dropped fields: names matching e-mail, phone, contact, fax, mobile, owner name, person (none matched in the 13 harvested files). uprn_suspect: a UPRN field with an exponent or 9+ digits ending in 5+ zeros (F22). The Brownfield Register is read from its CSV, not the GPKG (F23).

Network: one request at a time over the whole tool, at least 1.1 s apart; up to 6 tries with Retry-After or a doubling pause on 429, 5xx and network errors; User-Agent glitchcan-cwplans/0.1. robots.txt disallows only /debug, /manage/, /login, /logout.

rules: Box: BNG E 532400-539900, N 176700-182300 (fetch-docklands.mjs BOX_BNG); WGS84 to BNG through OSTN15; x = E - 537550, z = -(N - 180300); every value rounded to 0.5 m.

Ethics (CLAUDE.md, Data ethics): a tree keeps only position, taxon (scientific and common name), height, crown spread, source and record id. Notes, sponsorship, memorial, dedication, inscription, address, owner and maintainer fields are never read into the payload; each source lists its dropped fields in sources[].dropped.

Tree precedence: GLA public realm inventory first; then TPO points (planning.data), OSM natural=tree nodes and TOW Lone Tree crowns, each added only if no tree already kept lies within 3 m (TOW: within the crown radius, at least 3 m).
GLA class values ("05 to 10 m") become the middle of the class; "Not recorded" is null. Species "Unknown Tree Species" and common name "Plant" give no species.
TPO: records with an end date are left out; the taxon is read only from Tower Hamlets names of the form "Common (Scientific)"; Southwark names (site descriptions, URLs) are dropped.
OSM: species, else taxon, else genus (with the :en names); height under 60 m and diameter_crown under 40 m kept.
TOW Lone Tree: centroid of the polygon, height = maxht, crown = diameter of a circle with the polygon area (tow_area_m). Group of Trees, Small Woodland and NFI OHC polygons become greens with meanht.

Greens are clipped to the box (Sutherland-Hodgman) and simplified (Douglas-Peucker 0.5 m; TOW 1.5 m, its outlines follow the 1 m LiDAR grid); OSM multipolygon inner rings and shapefile holes are kept as holes.

activities.method: Trains a 3D Gaussian splat on the CPU with OpenSplat from a nerfstudio dataset, then converts the result to .splat (ply-to-splat.mjs) and .sog (splat-transform).
rules: Poses are passed to OpenSplat unchanged (OpenGL / nerfstudio camera-to-world; checked with splat-pose-test.py).
Defaults: 7000 iterations, image downscale 2, SH degree 3, at most 1,500,000 gaussians, refine every 500 steps.
activities.note: Child processes: opensplat, node ply-to-splat.mjs, splat-transform (falls back to 'npx -y @playcanvas/splat-transform', which downloads from npm when it is not installed). The log carries the run date.

used.note: a 3DGS training PLY (INRIA layout, binary little-endian, float properties)

activities.method: Converts a 3DGS PLY to the antimatter15 32-byte .splat format.
rules: scale = exp(log scale); rgb = 0.5 + SH_C0 x f_dc; alpha = sigmoid(opacity); quaternion normalised and stored as q x 128 + 128.
Sorted by exp(sum of log scales) x opacity, largest first; non-finite gaussians are dropped; f_rest is ignored.
activities.note: Called by train-splat.sh; also runs alone.

activities.method: Puts a trained splat set on the 3D page: crops it to the area the drone frames cover, drops floaters and oversized splats, and gives each splat its model building for the music visualiser.
rules: Keep splats within the box of the frame positions plus 150 m, between -30 and 260 m OD, with no axis over 25 m.
A splat belongs to a building when it lies inside the footprint (2 m grace) between the base - 2 m and the top + 6 m; else 65535.
Positions are not changed: train-splat.sh keeps the model frame (no --center).
activities.note: Run for the set cw-trained with data/raw/drone/cw-photo-480/first-n3000-d2.splat; another run adds its own set files.

activities.method: Runs 39 data-quality checks over every Canary Wharf source (identity, spatial, attribute, validity, parsing, network, timeliness, coverage, semantics) and writes one record per issue with counts, rates and examples, and a generated Markdown catalogue.
rules: Checks ID-1 to ID-5, SP-1 to SP-7, AT-1 to AT-5, VA-1 to VA-4, PL-1, PL-2, NET-1 to NET-5, TM-1 to TM-4, CV-1 to CV-4, SE-1 to SE-3.
The audit date is fixed in the code (2026-10-03): FSA ratings before 2023-10-03 are 'older than 3 years'; CWG copy ages are counted to that date.
VA-2 issues are the level tokens tools/osm-values.mjs cannot read (osmLevelsUnread).
Each issue has a severity (high, medium, low) and an entity (building, postcode, OSM element, FSA premises and others).

SP-2 leaves out occupants placed by a key (placed_confidence: SP-7). SP-6 counts an outline as the mall when its name, OSM name or addr:housename names it. CV-2 counts a CWG entry as seen by another source when a registry occupant from another source carries its URL after the registry join. CV-3: CWG entries the registry could not place, by reason.

CV-4: register records in the registry box with no building, by reason; ID-5: register UPRNs not used (shared across postcodes, or far from the register point); SE-3: register addresses that are not where the organisation works.
activities.judgement: Each new check is read by hand against its examples before it is trusted (curation skill, "Catalogue first").

used.endpoint: every url, api and sample URL in feeds/feeds.json
used.request: HTTP GET with Origin https://danbri.github.io; status, content type, CORS

activities.method: Re-checks every catalogued feed and prints its HTTP status and CORS answer, and where it differs from feeds.json.
rules: An api is fetched only when the source has no sample; CORS counts when Access-Control-Allow-Origin is * or the site origin.

Network: 6 workers, but at most one request at a time to a host and 1 s between requests to the same host, 30 s timeout, User-Agent glitchcan-cwplans/0.1, Origin https://danbri.github.io on api and sample requests; only the first chunk of each body is read. Nothing is written.

used.endpoint: every event and real-time feed URL in feeds/events.json
used.request: HTTP GET, with and without the Origin header; items and newest date by small generic parsers (ICS, RSS, Atom, JSON, schema.org Event JSON-LD)

activities.method: Re-checks the event and real-time feeds and prints status, CORS, item count, newest item date and the first titles.
rules: Item counts come from generic parsers and can differ from the hand-tuned samples in events.json.

Network: 6 workers, but at most one request at a time to a host and 1 s between requests to the same host, 30 s timeout, User-Agent glitchcan-cwplans/0.1; a second request with the Origin header tests CORS. Nothing is written.

activities.method: Checks the data register against the files git tracks (git ls-files) and the pages, and pipeline.json against the tools and files; exits 1 on a problem.
rules: Every tracked data file (not .mjs, .py, .c, .html, .gitignore, vendor/, skills/, the register and pipeline files) has a register entry; every entry's file exists.
Every source and OSM extract named is defined; osm.use agrees with the sources.
A page that loads a file holding OSM data (use raw, derived or counts) shows '© OpenStreetMap contributors' linked to https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright.

pipeline.json: every tracked tools/*, tools/native/*, tools/test/*, registry/sources/*/tools/*, registry/sources/*/* and feeds/* script (.mjs, .py, .sh, .c) is an activity, library or test; every tool, committed input and output exists; every source key is defined; every 'after' names an activity; every register file produced by a tools/ script is generated by an activity.
The repository paths in data-register.json osm_elsewhere_in_repo exist.

Every activity and every hand step (manual_activities) has a non-empty method and non-empty rules, an area that pipeline.json areas defines, and fault ids that the fault register in skills/docklands-data-curation/SKILL.md has; hand steps name only committed files and known sources.
activities.note: Child process: git ls-files. Run last, after every rebuild.

activities.method: Runs the same checks, then writes the readable register, the method catalogue (METHODS.md) and the provenance as JSON-LD for a knowledge graph.
rules: Activities become prov:Activity with prov:used and prov:generated; register files become prov:Entity and dcat:Distribution with prov:wasDerivedFrom their sources and prov:wasGeneratedBy the activity that generates them; sources become dcat:Dataset.
Committed files are identified by their GitHub URL, local files by urn:cwplans:local:<path>.

METHODS.md: methods-intro.md verbatim, then every activity by area (pipeline.json areas) in rebuild order (topological over after, ties in file order, a cycle in file order), the hand steps, the hand-judgement table, the fault register table read from the curation skill with the activities that cite each fault, the audit checks from quality/issues.json, the rebuild order, libraries and tests.
Hand steps (manual_activities) become prov:Activity with cwp:kind hand; area, faults and judgement are exported as cwp:area, cwp:fault and cwp:judgement.
activities.note: DATA-REGISTER.md and METHODS.md carry the run date.

manual_activities.what: Published levels used as tunnel and structure controls
manual_activities.method: Picks, from the cited facts in docklands/facts.json and from TfL freedom-of-information rail levels, the station, tunnel and structure levels that the 3D builds apply as controls, each with its datum, source URL and short quote.
rules: A level states its datum: od (metres above Ordnance Datum Newlyn) or below_ground (metres below the LiDAR ground at the point).
The asset owner's level (TfL rail level; London Underground Datum = OD - 100 m) outranks a rounded secondary depth; the loser stays in the file with superseded_by and is not applied (F13).
Each control names the line pattern and kinds of tunnel chain it applies to; structures name footprint_osm or water_name to be drawn from OSM.
Only short quotes are kept; plans and drawings are for reference by eye (feeds/underground/README.md).

manual_activities.what: Cited facts on the underground and multi-storey structure
manual_activities.method: Research agents collected 360 numeric facts (depths, tunnels, towers, docks, ground) with a source URL and a short quote each, and 19 recorded gaps; a script checked every quote against the cached copy of the page it cites (whitespace normalised); Wikidata values come from SPARQL with the statement as the quote. FACTS.md is the same facts as tables.
rules: Each fact keeps value, unit, datum, source URL and quote.
Datums are named: OD, CD (3.35 m below OD at West India Docks), mATD (OD + 100 m).
Gaps are recorded, not filled by guesses.
manual_activities.gap: The quote-check script and the FACTS.md generator were one-off scripts and are not committed: the method is recorded here, the code is not.

manual_activities.what: Source catalogue for the underground estate
manual_activities.method: Four research agents searched for plans, levels and 3D models of the malls, stations and tunnels; each entry was fetched directly or as an Internet Archive copy and its licence read; sources not used are listed with the reason. The README tables are generated from the JSON files.
rules: Nothing is copied into the model except cited level values (data/sourced-levels.json).
Copyright plans (Canary Wharf Group, TfL, Crossrail) are for reference by eye, not for copying.
Each exclusion records why (licence, no levels, duplicate, unreachable).
manual_activities.gap: The generator of feeds/underground/README.md is not committed.

manual_activities.what: Catalogue of live feeds, APIs and event sources
manual_activities.method: Research agents surveyed data sources in seven areas (341 added on 2026-10-03, 135 left out with reasons) and event, calendar, news and openings sources (124); each URL was fetched from the container and its status, CORS, licence and a sample recorded; check-feeds.mjs and check-events.mjs re-check them.
rules: Only official, published or openly licensed sources, and only cameras their owners publish for public viewing.
Left out with the reason: directories of unsecured private cameras, people-search and face-recognition sites, personal licence registers that list named individuals.
A source behind a bot challenge is "not verified", never "verified" (F11).
manual_activities.gap: The generators of feeds/README.md and feeds/EVENTS.md are not committed ("generated and by hand").
decisions_recorded_in: feeds/feeds.json and feeds/events.json (status, licence, excluded section)

manual_activities.what: Hand decisions on FSA and CWG brand matches
manual_activities.method: Matches that the rules cannot decide (an NSI prefix variant, an alternate name, a business type that does not fit the brand) are judged by hand, one record at a time, and written to decision files that the tools read on every run.
rules: A decision names the record, the brand item and accept or reject, with a reason.
Undecided and rejected matches are listed apart by the tools, never joined.

manual_activities.method: For branches whose OSM website is missing or a bare home page, the branch page was found by hand on the brand's own locator and its URL recorded; storelocator.mjs then checks it like any other.
rules: A URL on the brand's own domain; the UK site first.
Only the URL is recorded, not page content.

manual_activities.what: Open-licence subset of the museum and heritage records
manual_activities.method: Cuts records-open.json from records.json (fetch_records.py): records under CC0 (Wikidata), OGL (Historic England, OGL-licensed ADS records) or CC BY (Portable Antiquities Scheme), without the "sensitive" flag (burial or memorial context).
rules: Records flagged sensitive (44: burials, cemeteries, graves, memorials, skeletons) are left out (CLAUDE.md, Data ethics).
Records under other or unstated licences are left out.
manual_activities.gap: The cut was made by hand; no script in the repository writes records-open.json.

manual_activities.what: UKHO wrecks and obstructions clipped to the box
manual_activities.method: Clips the UKHO INSPIRE wrecks and obstructions shapefile to the Docklands box with ogr2ogr (the command is in registry/sources/pla/README.md).
rules: Depths (valsou) are metres below chart datum; not for navigation.

manual_activities.what: Open photos, facade regions and footprint widths for the facade measures
manual_activities.by: facade agent, then the main session
manual_activities.method: Searched Wikimedia Commons and Flickr for photos of the Canary Wharf towers, downloaded only CC0, Public Domain Mark and CC BY images, recorded author, licence, page and the face shown; chose a facade region in each photo by eye; computed oriented bounding boxes of the OSM footprints for face widths.
rules: CC BY-SA, NC, ND and all-rights-reserved images are not downloaded; seven CC BY-SA Commons photos were looked at for facts only.
The face shown is judged from landmarks when a photo has no geotag (32 of 45 Flickr photos).
Commons and Flickr rate-limit the container (429, retry after 600 s): wait, do not hammer.
decisions_recorded_in: registry/sources/facades/photos.json (face and how it was judged)

manual_activities.what: Pixel-art palette and music list for the 3D page
manual_activities.method: The pixel-art palette: 24 colours extracted from an owner-supplied reference picture by PIL median cut and k-means (a one-off run; the picture is not stored), plus 9 accent colours added by hand. The music list: tracks chosen by hand from Wikimedia Commons with title, artist, licence and page.
rules: Pixel-art colours do not follow height alone (owner, 2026-10-03: it reads as a heat map); materials carry the variety.
Music: CC BY 3.0 tracks (Kevin MacLeod) served by Wikimedia Commons with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, so the page can analyse them; the credit is shown while a track plays.
manual_activities.gap: The palette extraction was a one-off script and is not committed.

manual_activities.what: Licence check of every source before commit
manual_activities.by: hand (each session), owner decides open cases
manual_activities.method: Before a source is fetched into a committed file, its licence is read on the provider's own page and recorded in data-register.json sources (name, licence, attribution, note). Restricted, proprietary and share-alike sources other than OSM are not committed; open questions wait for the owner.
rules: Not committed: the VOA rating list (restricted licence), the PLA ArcGIS layers (no licence stated), the Canal & River Trust layers (no commercial use).
Not used: GLA canopy and green cover 2024 (all rights reserved), Curio Canopy (CC BY-SA), Wikipedia text (CC BY-SA), CC BY-SA Commons photos (looked at only).
Held for the owner: the Crossrail long section (licence not stated).
Needs an account, not fetched: HM Land Registry CCOD and OCOD, EPC data.
Re-check the Gambling Commission (no licence on the download page; data.gov.uk says OGL) before anything leaves prototyping.

manual_activities.what: Keeping pipeline.json and the register in step with the tools
manual_activities.method: Every new or changed tool updates its pipeline.json activity in the same commit (used, generated, method, rules, network, deterministic, after, area, faults, judgement); every new data file gets a data-register.json entry in the same commit; then check-data-register.mjs --write regenerates DATA-REGISTER.md, METHODS.md and pipeline.jsonld.
rules: The check fails on an unlisted tool, an empty method or rules, an unknown area or fault id, an unregistered data file, and a page that shows OSM data without the attribution link.
Source identifiers are kept as they come (OSM type/id, QID, UPRN, TOID, FHRS id, company number, cwb- id): they become IRIs.

manual_activities.what: Analysis of the error classes and the fault register
manual_activities.method: Reads the audit output, names the error class of each wrong value, writes the analysis and the proposed compositing layers, and records faults in our own joins and tools in the fault register with the measured effect of each fix.
rules: Catalogue first: name the class, add a check if none covers it; do not edit the record (owner, October 2026).
Change a tool only for a pipeline or join-rule fault; re-run the audit and compare the counts.

libraries.provides: HTTP get with the project User-Agent; QLever (paced, one call at a time, retried on 429 and 5xx) and query.wikidata.org SPARQL helpers; EA LiDAR WCS URLs; WGS84 to BNG through the OSTN15 grid (reads data/raw/uk_os_OSTN15_NTv2_OSGBtoETRS.tif); LiDAR tile mosaics; polygon helpers (area, point in polygon, box clip, cells, earcut mesh, ring joining, Douglas-Peucker, delta encoding); applyControls (published levels from data/sourced-levels.json as tunnel controls).

Paths for registry/sources and data/raw/registry; the Canary Wharf and Docklands boxes; cwPostcodes() (reads postcodes/postcodes.json; tiers cw-core, cw-ward, cw-box-other-ward, and terminated-cw unless told not to); postcode normaliser; CSV line splitter; sleep; inBox.
Parsers for OSM tag values: osmList (';' lists), unitLabel (adds 'Unit' to a bare designator), osmLevels (lists, comma lists, ranges, fractions) and osmLevelsUnread (tokens it cannot read).
Paths for the brands source (OUT, CW, RAW, NSI_DIR), the Canary Wharf box, One Canada Square, User-Agent, a require for the NSI packages installed in data/raw/registry/nsi, readJSON, sleep, inBox.

At import, builds the NSI Matcher over the brands/* tree with its location index (reads data/raw/registry/nsi/.../dist/json/nsi.json and featureCollection.json) and loads registry/sources/brands/brands-uk.json; exports matcher, brands, byId, byWd, KVS, hits(), nameVariants(), matchAny().

cwgFields (mall, level, postcode, district, street line and flags from CWG address lines), cwgLevelNum, nameKeys (name keys for joins: no accents or punctuation, "&" as "and", branch suffixes that name a place removed), CWG_PLACES, CWG_MALLS.

extractStructuredData(): self-contained in-page extractor for Playwright page.evaluate: JSON-LD script texts as found, HTML microdata as JSON (WHATWG algorithm, itemref followed), RDFa 1.1 (Core + HTML+RDFa rules) as N-Triples with the document base.

cleanJsonLd(raw): repairs one real-world JSON-LD block and counts each repair by class (HTML comment and CDATA wrappers, JS comments, trailing and missing commas, raw control characters, invalid escapes, concatenated values, HTML entities, remote schema.org contexts inlined, other remote contexts dropped, @graph unwrapped, http://schema.org/ normalised).

ECW decoder for build-aerial.py: decodes an ECW file to a PPM at every Nth pixel and prints its georeferencing as JSON. Built by hand against the ECW 3.3 SDK (curation skill, Imagery); the binary tools/native/ecw2ppm is gitignored.

tests.what: Fixture tests (node --test) for osmList, unitLabel, osmLevels and osmLevelsUnread in tools/osm-values.mjs.

Pose-convention test for the 3DGS trainer: 'gen OUT' writes a synthetic nerfstudio dataset of coloured boxes on a chequered ground with known OpenGL camera-to-world matrices (images, transforms.json, sparse_pc.ply; --init grey, --flip opencv as a negative control); 'points OUT N' rewrites sparse_pc.ply with about N points; 'check PLY' reports per box how many opaque gaussians of a trained PLY lie inside it and their mean colour. Needs numpy and Pillow.

Fixture tests (node --test) for cwgFields, cwgLevelNum and nameKeys in registry/sources/brands/tools/cwg-fields.mjs, including the parse faults of the first fetch-cwg ("United Kingdom" and "55 Upper Bank Street" as levels).
Fixture tests (node --test) for cleanJsonLd in tools/jsonld-clean.mjs, including the bigeasy.co.uk missing-comma block of 2026-10-03.
